source.adaptation: Baryon transcribed only the historical 2021 and 2025 columns, renamed Other within the clean-energy breakdown for clarity, and calculates rounding differences. Original values and units are preserved.
source.permissionScope: IEA analysis table on page 347, with no third-party credit on that table. No logos, photographs, cover, other tables, underlying third-party datasets or report PDF are redistributed.

method.description: The IEA combines technology activity, technology mix and material intensity assumptions for energy uses; other uses draw on historical end-use consumption, activity indicators and material intensities. These historical columns are publisher assessments, not independent Baryon measurements.
dependencies: Global Energy and Climate model and energy-technology activity inputs
Literature, expert and industry input to material intensities
Historical end-use consumption and activity drivers for non-energy demand; table-level upstream independence unresolved
method.evScope: Electric-vehicle battery and motor demand are both included.
method.constructionScope: The model focuses on material required to build plants and equipment, rather than their operating fuel requirements.

scope: Only 2021 and 2025 historical estimates are admitted; 2030, 2040 and 2050 scenario columns are excluded.
Clean-energy components belong inside the clean-energy total; do not add them to total demand again.
Global refined-copper demand cannot establish regional unmet demand or available procurement supply.
Direct-use scrap is excluded; do not equate this boundary with US apparent consumption that includes old-scrap direct melt.
Keep printed whole-kt quantities and whole-percent shares; preserve rounding residuals rather than forcing closure.
